name: SAMURAI (Yang et al., arXiv 2411.11922) and UncTrack (arXiv 2503.12888) - memory writing gated by motion and uncertainty checks
bibliography: (1) Cheng-Yen Yang, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Wenhao Chai, Zhongyu Jiang, Jenq-Neng Hwang (University of Washington). SAMURAI: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Zero-Shot Visual Tracking with Motion-Aware Memory. arXiv:2411.11922, v2 30 Nov 2024 (preprint; the arXiv page lists no venue). HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.11922v2 ; code: https://github.com/yangchris11/samurai (fork of SAM 2 with samurai_mode; config sam2/sam2/configs/samurai/sam2.1_hiera_l.yaml, logic in sam2/sam2/modeling/sam2_base.py). (2) Siyuan Yao, Yang Guo, Yanyang Yan, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao. UncTrack: Reliable Visual Object Tracking with Uncertainty-Aware Prototype Memory Network. arXiv:2503.12888 v1, 17 Mar 2025 (preprint, no venue on the arXiv page). HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.12888 ; code: https://github.com/ManOfStory/UncTrack. No duplicate records (no journal versions found for either within this check).
full_text_checked: SAMURAI: full HTML v2 (method, Tables 1-4, attribute analysis) plus code: config yaml (thresholds) and sam2_base.py (Kalman branch in _forward_sam_heads, memory selection loop in _prepare_memory_conditioned_features) read via raw GitHub. UncTrack: full HTML v1 (method, Tables I-IX, ablations, failure cases); parts of the HTML are garbled (loss weights, top-k value); code repository not inspected. Supplementary material for neither paper was examined.
task_and_output: Both are single-object visual trackers (VOT) given the first-frame target. SAMURAI outputs a segmentation mask per frame (box derived from mask min/max) built on SAM 2.1; among the 3 multimask candidates of SAM 2 it selects one using a Kalman-IoU + mask-affinity score. UncTrack outputs a bounding box via corner probability maps, a per-coordinate uncertainty (Gaussian sigma for 4 corner coordinates) and a 2-way reliability score from a prototype memory network.
data_and_independent_videos: SAMURAI: training-free (zero-shot on SAM 2.1 weights); evaluated on LaSOT (280 test videos), LaSOText (150), GOT-10k test, TrackingNet, NFS, OTB100 - all standard test splits unseen by SAM 2 training as far as the paper states. UncTrack: trained on TrackingNet, LaSOT, GOT-10k, COCO train splits; tested on LaSOT, TrackingNet, GOT-10k, VOT2020, UAV123, OTB100, NAT2021 (standard test splits; GOT-10k ablations on GOT-10k test which has unseen classes).
target_size_and_input_resolution: SAMURAI: SAM 2.1 image_size 1024 (from config sam2.1_hiera_l.yaml; paper does not state it); full frame processed, targets of benchmark sizes (typically tens to hundreds of pixels). UncTrack-B: template 128x128, search 288x288; UncTrack-L: template 192x192, search 384x384 (search region several times target size). Neither reports performance by small target size explicitly.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Benchmark native frame rates (mostly 25-30 fps; NFS 30-fps version). SAMURAI attribute analysis shows the largest gains on camera motion and fast motion. Background motion is not modeled separately; the Kalman filter is a linear constant-velocity box model in image coordinates.
detector_and_exemplar: No external detector. SAMURAI: exemplar = first-frame box prompt; SAM 2 memory bank of past frames (num_maskmem 7) acts as dynamic exemplar set. UncTrack: static template from first frame plus a FIFO bank of 6 prototypes from reliable past frames; on low confidence the template is re-sampled from the nearest reliable frame.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: SAMURAI: none trained; hand-designed Kalman filter and thresholds on top of frozen SAM 2.1 (Tiny/Small/Base/Large, ViT Hiera). UncTrack: stage 1 trains MAE-pretrained ViT encoder + uncertainty-aware localization decoder (500 epochs) with CIoU + L1 + KL-based uncertainty loss ((mu-mu_gt)^2/(2 sigma^2) + log(sigma^2)/2; weights garbled in HTML); stage 2 freezes encoder/decoder and trains prototype memory network 50 epochs with cross-entropy on a 2-way reliability output. Params (Table VII): UncTrack-B 109.3M (95.99M without ULD/PMN), UncTrack-L 310.0M (286.8M without).
controls_seeds_splits: SAMURAI: matched baseline = same SAM 2.1 weights without motion/memory selection, for 4 model sizes (Tables 1-2); 2x2 component ablation (motion, memory) on LaSOT (Table 3); motion weight sweep (Table 4). Single deterministic run, no seeds, no confidence intervals. UncTrack: component ablation (baseline/+ULD/+PMN/both) on GOT-10k (Table IV); memory type replacement STM/LSTM/GRU (Table V); MAE ablation (Table VI); threshold T sweep on VOT2020 (Table VIII); memory size sweep (Fig. 6). Single runs, no seeds or intervals reported.

Table 4 alpha_kf: 0 -> 72.67, 0.15 -> 74.23, 0.25 -> 73.76, 0.50 -> 72.92 (text claims 0.2 best; code config uses kf_score_weight 0.15). Tables 1: LaSOT AUC baseline->SAMURAI T 66.70->69.28, S 66.47->70.04, B 65.97->70.65, L 68.54->74.23; LaSOText T 52.25->55.13, S 56.11->57.99, B 55.51->57.48, L 58.55->61.03. GOT-10k AO SAMURAI-L 81.7. Table 2 SAMURAI-L AUC: TrackingNet 85.3, NFS 69.2, OTB100 71.5. Attribute analysis (LaSOText): illumination variation decreases (B -2.3, L -3.5); background clutter +15.7 for B. Code (config sam2.1_hiera_l.yaml): stable_frames_threshold 15, stable_ious_threshold 0.3, kf_score_weight 0.15, memory_bank_iou_threshold 0.5, memory_bank_obj_score_threshold 0.0, memory_bank_kf_score_threshold 0.0, num_maskmem 7. UncTrack (arXiv 2503.12888v1): Table IV GOT-10k AO/SR0.5/SR0.75 UncTrack-B: baseline 74.3/84.1/73.0; +ULD 75.1/84.5/74.6; +PMN 75.3/84.5/74.9; both 75.6/85.1/75.2. LaSOT attributes (text): full occlusion success 0.648 (L), out-of-view 0.682 (L), background clutter 0.647 (L).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (standard test splits; SAMURAI zero-shot). Target absence: no dedicated evaluation in either paper (only LaSOT out-of-view / full-occlusion attributes in UncTrack, LaSOT/LaSOText attributes in SAMURAI). Similar distractors: SAMURAI qualitative only (Fig. 4) and background-clutter attribute; UncTrack none dedicated, failure cases with similar objects acknowledged. Occlusion: attribute-level only (both). Night/low light: not reported; SAMURAI illumination-variation attribute on LaSOText decreases. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes, both run causally online on their own outputs.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism, SAMURAI: (a) a linear Kalman filter on box [x,y,w,h + velocities] predicts the box; each of SAM 2's three candidate masks is scored as 0.15*IoU(candidate box, KF prediction) + 0.85*predicted mask IoU; the highest wins and updates the filter. (b) Motion scoring is only enabled after 15 consecutive frames with predicted mask IoU > 0.3; any frame below 0.3 resets the counter and re-initialises the filter. (c) Memory: past frames are kept as memory only if predicted mask IoU > 0.5 and object-presence logit > 0.0 (and motion score > 0.0 in the paper); up to 6 such frames plus the previous frame are used. Code finding: the memory loop reads key 'kf_score' while track_step stores 'kf_ious', so the motion check on memory write is never applied in the released code (threshold 0.0 anyway); the memory gain is thus from mask-IoU and object-score gating. Published mechanism, UncTrack: the localization head predicts a Gaussian sigma per box corner; a confidence-inversion module turns uncertainty into features fused with search features; a prototype (pooled masked feature) is written FIFO into a 6-slot memory only if a learned 2-way reliability score > 0.5; low reliability triggers template re-sampling from the nearest reliable frame, doubled search area and Kalman motion consistency. Proposed modification (ours, not published): gate the FlyVis readout correction and its exemplar update by a self-check combining FlyVis map agreement with a motion prior, recorded only when consistent over several frames.
transfer_limits: (1) SAMURAI's selection is among 3 SAM-2 mask hypotheses whose quality scores come from a large RGB foundation model; our candidates are 3 peaks of a FlyVis target-model map on 721 grey hexals with no learned quality score - we already have Kalman-based candidate selection as a control (C_kalman/D_kalman in z13_candidate_ranker_v1, z13_map_only104_v1). (2) The motion gate needs 15 stable frames before it acts; our loss episodes start exactly when the track is lost, with 4 exemplar observations, so the gate would mostly be off - in our setting the Kalman prior is the ByteTrack prediction itself, i.e. the crop centre, so a KF term pulls the correction to zero shift. (3) The crop is centred on and rescaled with the prediction at 30 Hz; KF-IoU in crop coordinates is mostly a distance-to-centre penalty, which is a shift limit - an external guard rule. (4) Targets ~9x12 lattice steps occupy a window twice the target; neighbours are within the same crop, so distractors are as close to the prediction as the target. (5) UncTrack's uncertainty head is trained with 4 large datasets and a 96M-param ViT; its gain over baseline is +1.3 AO on GOT-10k (Table IV) - small, and no evidence for tiny feature sets. (6) Neither paper measures refusal when the target is absent among similar neighbours, which is our main decision. (7) Our environment (YOLO26s + ByteTrack + MASA) already contains a Kalman filter; SAMURAI's motion term therefore duplicates the stand.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1 (right object and refusal): design analogy and caution - SAMURAI combines appearance quality with motion for selection but has no refusal; UncTrack's reliability score is a learned presence/quality classifier; neither separates 'similar distractor' from 'target'. 5.2 (target model and memory): direct evidence that memory-write gating gives the larger part of the gain (SAMURAI Table 3: memory selection +4.35 AUC vs motion +2.49 on LaSOT, rich RGB features). UncTrack: gated prototype memory +1.0 AO (Table IV). 5.3 (core training through applied readout): not addressed (SAMURAI training-free; UncTrack trains memory with frozen backbone). 5.4 (association): caution - motion gating equals an external Kalman guard; any effect must be separated with a no-fly Kalman control.
candidate_node_change: Node: state transfer / exemplar update of the FlyVis readout (not the core). Change: write a new exemplar observation into the observation memory only after a self-check - centred readout response at the chosen peak above a fixed quantile, peak agreement between C and D readouts, and displacement consistent with the ByteTrack Kalman prediction within a fixed Mahalanobis gate; enable the motion term only after k consecutive passes. Controls: (a) stand without correction; (b) same gate using Kalman displacement only (no FlyVis, choose detection nearest to KF prediction) - the required no-fly control; (c) stock FlyVis features (R1/eye input) with the same gate; (d) modernised FlyVis C/D with the gate. Minimal check: on saved train26 episodes, compare useful/harmful counts of applied corrections at a fixed 1% intervention quota against z13_balanced_ridge_v1 and the C_kalman control; no HOTA. Stop condition: if (d) is not better than (b) with paired-bootstrap CI lower bound > 0, or useful share among selected corrections stays below the existing 2/84 level, stop; do not tune gates on dev35. Expected value: low, because the gate mostly reduces to a shift limit (see z13_first_divergence_v1, 79.7 px shift).
strongest_objection: SAMURAI's measurable gain comes from selecting memory frames with SAM 2's own learned mask-IoU and object-presence heads on rich RGB features; the motion part is a plain Kalman filter that the stand already has. Transferred to FlyVis, the remaining novel element is only a threshold rule, which is an external guard rule rather than a FlyVis modernization, and its effect would be obtainable without FlyVis. In addition the code does not implement the motion check on memory writing as described, so the paper's 'three checks' claim is weaker than written, and none of the numbers has a confidence interval.
evidence_strength: Both preprints (no peer-reviewed venue verified). SAMURAI: code public and inspected; widely re-used (many follow-ups, e.g. DAM4SAM compares to it) [uncertain]; single runs, no CI; text/table inconsistencies (alpha 0.2 vs 0.15; Pnorm 82.60 vs 82.69). UncTrack: code link public, not inspected; small ablation gains (+1.3 AO), single runs. Overall: moderate for SAMURAI's ablation direction on RGB benchmarks; weak for transfer to our setting; weak for UncTrack.
where_distinction_is_made: SAMURAI: no explicit four-way distinction. 'Target found vs similar object' is decided implicitly in a separate selection step (weighted KF-IoU + SAM mask-IoU over 3 candidates); 'target absent/occluded' via SAM 2's object-presence logit (representation + learned head), used only to gate memory and suppress the mask; 'insufficient data' via the 15-stable-frame counter that disables motion. A map maximum is not equated with presence: presence is a separate learned logit. UncTrack: distinction made by a separate learned reliability head on prototype-memory features (2-way cross-entropy) and by predicted localization uncertainty; target absent vs distractor are not separated - both fall into 'unreliable'.
feature_dependence: Strongly dependent on large RGB backbones: SAMURAI uses SAM 2.1 Hiera ViT features and SAM's learned mask-IoU and object-score heads (memory gate thresholds are on these outputs); UncTrack uses an MAE-pretrained ViT (96-287M params) and reports drops without MAE pretraining (Table VI, e.g. TrackingNet AUC 85.0 -> 83.3 for B). No evidence that the mechanisms work with small temporal motion/brightness features. Only the Kalman component is feature-independent.
association_consequence: Not linked to MOT association in either paper. In our setting the effect of SAMURAI's motion term is equivalent to penalising corrections far from the ByteTrack prediction - an external shift limit or cost check (e.g. reject a correction if it raises the IoU cost of the best matching detection above 0.8) would give the same effect without the mechanism, as our case R1 shows (79.7 px shift raising cost 0.123 -> 1.0, z13_first_divergence_v1).
difference_from_tried: Ranking of 3 peaks (z13_candidate_ranker_v1, z13_map_only104_v1): already included a Kalman-based selection control (C_kalman/D_kalman); SAMURAI's weighted KF + quality score is a linear blend of what we tried separately - small difference (blending weight), no new mechanism. Absolute confidence (z13_absolute_confidence_v1): SAMURAI uses a learned quality (mask-IoU) score rather than raw map height - difference only if FlyVis had a learned quality head; our utility heads on map/geometry (z13_map_utility_v1, z13_next_utility_v1) are the closest analogue and failed (2 useful of 84 selected). Observation memory (z13_observed_memory_v1) and query memory (z13_query_memory_v1): real difference is the write rule - SAMURAI/UncTrack write only frames that pass a quality gate, whereas our memories stored the 4 exemplar observations unconditionally; however during loss episodes there are no new verified observations to write, so the difference has little scope in Z13. UncTrack's learned uncertainty is a new element (heteroscedastic localization variance) not tried by us.
memory_write_policy: SAMURAI (code): a past frame enters memory if predicted mask IoU > 0.5 and object-score logit > 0.0; motion check (> 0.0) intended but inactive due to key mismatch; scan backwards until 15 valid frames for object pointers, last 6 valid + previous frame used as mask memory; first conditioning frame always kept. UncTrack: prototype written FIFO into 6 slots only if reliability > T = 0.5 (T 0.7/0.9 slightly worse on VOT2020).
distractor_representation: Implicit only. SAMURAI: distractors appear as alternative SAM mask candidates, not stored. UncTrack: no distractor buffer; only via training loss.
refusal_evidence_horizon: SAMURAI: single-frame object-score logit for presence; motion enabling uses accumulation over 15 frames. UncTrack: single-frame reliability score. No sequential test.
loss_on_applied_decision: SAMURAI: no loss (training-free). UncTrack: reliability head trained with cross-entropy on a reliability label (not on the memory-write decision or tracking outcome); localization loss on box corners - intermediate to the applied template-update decision.
association_entry_point: Not applicable to MOT in the sources. If transferred: state update (whether a FlyVis correction / exemplar is written) and box correction after matching gate; it would not enter the matching cost directly.
no_fly_control_equivalent: Kalman motion gating already in ByteTrack: choose the detection/peak nearest to the Kalman prediction, or reject corrections exceeding a Mahalanobis/shift limit; IoU-cost check of the corrected centre against the best detection. The project's existing C_kalman/D_kalman arms (z13_candidate_ranker_v1, z13_map_only104_v1) are the direct no-fly controls; a shift-limit rule is the second.
hard_subset_evaluation: No dedicated hard subset. SAMURAI reports LaSOT/LaSOText attribute subsets (camera motion, fast motion, background clutter, illumination variation) defined by benchmark annotations; UncTrack reports LaSOT attributes (occlusion, out-of-view, background clutter) in text. Not DiDi, DanceTrack or MOSE.
temporal_information_availability: Both strictly causal: decisions use current and past frames only, answer available in the current frame with no extra latency (SAMURAI reports real-time on RTX 4090 without fps numbers; UncTrack reports no fps). SAMURAI's motion term needs 15 past stable frames before activation, i.e. a warm-up delay of about 0.5 s at 30 fps after each reset.
depth_level: Full analysis (as set in the item). Conclusion: the useful part (gated memory writing) is the same family as DAM4SAM (N16); the motion part duplicates the stand's Kalman filter and is covered by existing controls. Not recommended as the next implementation; usable as a design note for the write rule and as the source of the mandatory Kalman no-fly control.
